text:
maya: noticed a new p99 tail after yesterday's runtime tweak (kernel selector + slight microbatch change). p95 looks fine, p99 jumped ~1.8x on 8k workloads. anyone else see this?
eric: yup saw it in prod graphs ~08:15UTC. correlates with the rollout to the "fast-kernel-election" flag.
maya: attaching a quick flame from trace sampling. looks like a small set of requests spend a long time in kernel fallback and then hit a tool-call loop which exacerbates.
olivia: can you paste the profiler snippet?
maya: sure — sampled 100 traces, here's the condensed stack + timing (ns):
```
SERVE_LOOP  12000000
 -> kernel_select 800000
 -> run_fused_attn_v2 200000
 -> fallback_slow_path 2800000
 -> kv_cache_miss_recon 900000
 -> tool_call_dispatch 6000000
```
maya: note fallback_slow_path is big on these traces. the kernel selection took 800us deciding, then fallback fired.
kai: interesting — fallback_slow_path and kv_cache_miss_recon together look like cache thrash when context > 6k. we've been changing batch packing heuristics to favor throughput so microbatch size bumped to 8 in some paths. that could worsen KV lookups and evictions.
eric: i reran a repro locally with microbatch=1 and microbatch=8. p99 for the long prompt shape: microbatch=1 -> 250ms p99, microbatch=8 -> 430ms p99. p95 delta small.
olivia: that pattern matches throughput vs latency tradeoff. but why kernel_select is so slow? selector should be O(1) heuristics.
maya: found the culprit — we added a new heuristics step that runs a small profiling kernel if sequence length > 4k to pick quantized vs fp16 kernels. that profiling path calls into cuBLAS warmup and can block async queues when combined with certain batch layouts.
olivia: can you show the selector diff?
maya: snippet from git: `if seq_len > 4096: run_light_profile(); if profile.latency_est > threshold -> choose_fallback`. the light_profile uses a single-sample cuBLAS matmul to get timing.
kai: that explains it. light_profile is not async-safe with concurrent microbatches; it stalls the kernel scheduler causing visible stalls at p99. combine that with KV eviction due to larger microbatch packing and tool calls that re-enter the runtime and do sync I/O -> disaster.
olivia: proposals: 1) make profiling path non-blocking (offload to separate stream + timeout), 2) gate the profiler behind microbatch size (only run for microbatch==1 or sample 1/1000), 3) revert the rollout for the flag while we patch.
eric: also saw tool_call_dispatch loops: some generator outputs trigger a tool call, tool returns appended prompt, generator resumes and hits the long context path again -> nested tool-call cycles. that multiplies the effect.
maya: example payload: user prompt 7k tokens, model generates "CALL_TOOL": tool returns 1.5k tokens appended, generator resumes with 8.5k context and triggers kernel reselect + KV recompute. repeat.
benchbot: load test note: synthetic replay with 7k base prompt + tool echo increased p99 3x under microbatch=8 compared to microbatch=1.
olivia: immediate mitigation: disable selector profiling for seq_len>4k and set microbatch default back to 2 for that rollout group. also add a fast-path to avoid kernel reselect if KV cache contains a valid cached prefix mapping.
kai: for longer term: 1) move profiling to an async sampled actor with CPC budget, 2) ensure kernel_select is pure-deterministic cheap fallthrough for common shapes, 3) add a guard against repeated tool-call-induced reselects (e.g., mark request as "pinned_kernel") and reuse the decided kernels for nested resumes.
eric: I'll open a quick PR to revert the rollout flag and add a gating check. maya can you craft a short test that reproduces the tool-call loop? benchbot can run it on preprod with microbatch params.
maya: test plan: script that replays 1k requests: base_prompt=7000 tokens, on gen step emit TOOL_CALL every 20 tokens, tool echoes back 1500 tokens. test cases: microbatch=1,2,4,8 and selector profiling enabled/disabled. will post script here shortly.
benchbot: scheduled run on preprod (r32-gpu-pool) starting in 10m. I'll attach aggregates after run.
olivia: thanks everyone. keep the thread for updates — major priority until rollback/patch landed. :thumbsup:
